headline: COLLECTIVE MINING DOUBLES RAMP ZONE TO 720M VERTICAL — 21.4M AT 11.06 G/T AUEQ AT GUAYABALES TODAY
snippet: Collective Mining (NYSE/TSX: CNL) reported that directional diamond drilling at the Ramp Zone of its Apollo deposit in Colombia's Guayabales project has more than doubled the zone's vertical extent to approximately 720 metres, from about 350 metres in the current Mineral Resource. The headline intercept — 21.40 metres at 11.06 g/t AuEq — came from one of four new holes, all confirming that high-grade mineralization continues well beyond the existing resource envelope in a district already hosting one of the most significant recent gold-copper discoveries in South America.

headline: MMG PUSHES EU TO CLEAR $500M ANGLO AMERICAN NICKEL DEAL — ANTITRUST DOUBTS SLOW ACQUISITION
snippet: Chinese state-linked miner MMG is actively lobbying European competition regulators to approve its $500 million acquisition of Anglo American's nickel assets, with a crunch EU meeting on November 9 addressing concerns the deal could cut ferronickel supply to European stainless steel producers. The EU probe follows MMG's withdrawal of its simplified-procedure application; the American Iron and Steel Institute has separately urged Washington to block the deal over fears Beijing would gain direct control of significant global nickel reserves.

headline: SUPER COPPER HITS COPPER IN EVERY HOLE AT EL ALTO — MAIDEN CHILE DRILL RETURNS UP TO 2.56% CUEQ
snippet: Super Copper (CSE: CUPR) reported first assays from its maiden drilling program at the El Alto project in Chile's Atacama Region, with copper-bearing mineralization returned in every hole along the main northwest-trending structure and a headline interval of up to 2.56% copper equivalent. A 100% hit rate on a maiden program in one of the world's premier copper jurisdictions marks a strong opening chapter for a project still in early-stage exploration.

headline: FIREFLY METALS EXTENDS MING MINE HIGH-GRADE CORE — 16.4M AT 9.2% CUEQ IN NEWFOUNDLAND VMS SYSTEM
snippet: FireFly Metals (TSX-V: FFM) released drilling results from the Ming Mine copper-zinc-gold-silver VMS deposit in Newfoundland showing the high-grade core zone extending laterally, with headline intercepts of 16.4 metres at 9.2% CuEq and 15.5 metres at 12.4% CuEq. VMS grades of this magnitude in a laterally-growing core zone represent strong resource addition potential at an advanced project with existing underground infrastructure — exactly the kind of near-term resource growth that moves the needle on project economics.

headline: GOLD X2 MINING DRILLS 258.4M AT 0.97 G/T AU AND 192M AT 0.90 G/T — QES EXTENSION CONFIRMS UNDERGROUND CASE
snippet: Gold X2 Mining (TSX-V: AUXX) reported two QES zone extension drill holes at its Moss Gold Project in Northwest Ontario returning 258.4 metres at 0.97 g/t Au and 192.0 metres at 0.90 g/t Au — broad intercepts confirming the mineralized shear zone continues well below the current open-pit shell. The company says the results support an underground mining scenario beyond the existing NI 43-101 resource, expanding project value at a time when gold prices above $4,000/oz transform bulk tonnage deposits that were marginal at $1,800 gold into genuinely economic underground targets.

headline: RADISSON EXTENDS HIGH-GRADE GOLD AT O'BRIEN — 83% STEP-OUT HIT RATE FROM 140,000M PROGRAM HOLDS
snippet: Radisson Mining (TSX-V: RDS) released new drill results from its 140,000-metre step-out program at the former O'Brien Gold Mine in Québec's Abitibi gold belt, extending high-grade mineralization to depth and laterally with 83% of all step-out holes returning significant intercepts across a system now spanning over 1,000 vertical metres. Prior highlights include a 68.24 g/t gold over 6.2 metres intercept and the project's highest-ever assay of 1,604 g/t over 1 metre — a hit-rate and grade consistency that remains exceptional for a non-resource step-out campaign.

headline: COPPERNICO CLEARS FINAL DRILL PERMIT AT SOMBRERO PERU — MULTI-TARGET PROGRAM OUTLINED IN PORPHYRY BELT
snippet: Coppernico Metals received its final drill permit at the Sombrero copper-gold project in Peru and outlined a multi-target drilling program, with historical surface work returning anomalies including 90.4 metres of 0.48% copper and 0.05 g/t gold in historical drill holes. The permit clears the last regulatory hurdle before drilling commences on a project located in the same Andean porphyry copper belt that hosts some of Peru's largest producing mines.

headline: STANDARD CHARTERED: GOLD MUST HOLD $3,886 OR RISK DEEPER CORRECTION — OIL SPIKE FUELS DECEMBER HIKE BETS
snippet: Standard Chartered's metals research team identified $3,886 per troy ounce as the key technical and fundamental support level for gold, warning that a break below it — driven by oil-fueled inflation and rising Fed rate-hike odds — risks triggering a deeper correction beyond today's CPI-driven selloff to $4,053. The bank maintains its $4,650 Q4 2026 and $4,850 Q1 2027 forecasts but flags the December FOMC meeting as the decisive near-term risk event, with December hike probabilities now firmly above 80%.

headline: SILVER LAGS GOLD ON FED HIKE FEARS — $48-$50 SUPPORT ZONE NOW IN PLAY AS INDUSTRIAL DEMAND SIGNALS FADE
snippet: FX Empire's precious metals analysis finds silver significantly underperforming gold in the November selloff — falling nearly 2.9% to test critical $48-$50 support — as 75% of market participants now price a December Fed rate hike. Silver's higher sensitivity to industrial demand means it carries a dual burden: precious metals headwinds from rate hike fears plus industrial exposure to a potential economic slowdown, making the $48-$50 band a critical technical test for investors considering entry on weakness.

headline: GOLD MINERS ROSE WHILE GOLD FELL FRIDAY — GDXJ +2.8% SIGNALS SECTOR MAY BE PRICING IN A BOTTOM
snippet: Gold mining stocks bucked the metal's Friday decline, with the junior gold ETF GDXJ rising 2.8% even as spot gold fell $38.60 on strong U.S. jobs data — a rare divergence that analysts are watching as a potential leading indicator of a sector bottom. One featured analyst still expects gold to test $3,500 before reversing, arguing that miners usually lead the metal higher at genuine cycle lows; the GDXJ outperformance against gold's fifth consecutive down-week may be the first evidence that institutional money is positioning ahead of that reversal.
